messages:
maria: Heads up — started a strict-validate fncall canary in eu-west a few mins ago. Seeing a ~3x spike in reject events and a small billing blip. filing this thread to coordinate quick mitigations
kevin: ack. can you paste a sample event from the telemetry stream? curious if these are hard rejects vs soft validations
maria: sample event below (sanitized):
```json
{
  "route_id": "payments-processor",
  "model": "gptx-1",
  "fncall_name": "charge_card",
  "validation_result": "reject",
  "reject_type": "schema_mismatch",
  "validation_mode": "strict",
  "timestamp": 4819237654,
  "billing_charge_usd": 0.0023
}
```
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: validation_reject_rate for route payments-processor exceeded 5/min at 4819237662 (canary=true). Linked runbook: https://internal/redwood/runbooks/validation-spikes
ux-anna: For console rollouts view — do we currently show soft vs hard validation counts separately? customers keep asking why canary shows traffic but lots of rejects in the events table
maria: no, console surfaces a single "validation_failures" metric. UX folks asked for split but we never implemented dims for validation_mode or reject_type in dash panels
sanjay: propose 2 quick mitigations: 1) add a canary safelist of allowed fncall names for strict mode so only vetted adapters are exercised, 2) tag telemetry with validation_mode so console can split soft vs hard counts. something like:
```yaml
canary_config:
  strict_mode: true
  fncall_safelist: ["lookup_user", "charge_card"]
```
kevin: adding validation_mode to the telemetry v2 event is quick (I can land a PR). For the safelist we need policy enforcement at the router layer — I want to avoid invasive runtime changes during a canary
maria: router-level quick patch: if canary=true and strict_mode=true then reject any fncall not in safelist with a soft-fallback that returns an explanation instead of hitting downstream adapters. That reduces adapter error noise + billing. We can flip to hard reject after we verify adapter behavior
ux-anna: console change request: add a small donut that breaks out validation_mode=soft|strict and reject_type (schema_mismatch, parse_error, unknown_fn). Also expose canary tag so SREs can scope to canary runs. I'll sketch mockups
sanjay: routing fallback suggestion: route to "degen" variant if safelist miss, but mark returned payload with fields `{ validation_fallback: true, fallback_reason: \"fn-not-allowed\" }` so app-level consumers know it was a policy fallback
kevin: I'll do telemetry PR (events + new dimension). maria — can you open the router PR for safelist enforcement? sanjay — can you spec the fallback payload schema so we don't accidentally break clients
maria: opening router PR now, will include a canary toggle flag and an escape hatch env var. linking here when done
maria: PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/router/pulls/4821 — contains config + tests for safelist + soft-fallback behavior
ops-bot: Deploy bot: canary patch deployed to eu-west-1 at 4819237684 by deploy-ci. status: success :white_check_mark:
kevin: telemetry PR up next, will wire sampling & new dashboard dims. rough alert idea: if strict-mode hard rejects > 0.1% of requests for 5min then page oncall
ux-anna: I'll add console mock to the rollout dashboard and hide the split behind "show validation detail" until we get PM signoff
sanjay: I'll produce the fallback payload spec in the RFC doc, include schema example and compatibility notes
maria: thanks everyone. initial numbers look calmer after safelist went live — rejects down ~70% (still watching). ping me if anything spikes :thumbsup:
